content.user_title: Build Azure Content Safety Java Moderation
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable patterns for harmful content detection. This skill shows Azure AI Content Safety client setup, analysis flows, and blocklist operations.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for the Azure AI Content Safety Java SDK.
Demonstrates ContentSafetyClient and BlocklistClient creation with an API key or DefaultAzureCredential.
Explains harm categories and severity scales for text and image analysis.
Provides text analysis patterns with selected categories, output levels, and blocklist hits.
Provides image analysis examples from local image bytes and a blob URL.
Covers blocklist create, update, list, add, remove, and delete operations.
limitations: Does not include a complete runnable Java project or build configuration.
Uses sample text, image URLs, and blocklist names that must be replaced.
Does not cover deployment, monitoring, or moderation policy governance in depth.
SDK version and API behavior should be checked against the target Azure environment.

use_cases.title: Add Comment Moderation
use_cases.description: Build a Java service that checks user comments for hate, violence, sexual content, and self-harm severity.

use_cases.title: Manage Custom Blocklists
use_cases.description: Create, update, list, and remove terms that your moderation policy must block or review.

use_cases.title: Design Moderation Controls
use_cases.description: Compare SDK authentication, category selection, severity thresholds, and operational tradeoffs before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Java moderation service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the Azure AI Content Safety Java client setup for API key authentication. Include required environment variables and the main client classes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze User Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Moderate text using selected harm categories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Java text moderation flow for user comments. Include category selection, severity output, and how to handle blocklist matches.

prompt_templates.title: Moderate Images
prompt_templates.scenario: Add image safety checks to a Java service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how to analyze images with Azure AI Content Safety in Java. Cover local image bytes and URL-based image input.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Blocklist Operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced blocklist lifecycle and policy design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create an implementation plan for custom text blocklists. Include creation, item updates, listing, removal, deletion, and operational delay handling.

output_examples.input: I need a Java moderation service for user comments.
output_examples.output: A setup outline covering the Maven package, environment variables, client creation, text analysis categories, severity handling, and blocklist checks.

output_examples.input: I need to manage blocked words for a trust and safety policy.
output_examples.output: A blocklist workflow explaining how to create a list, add terms, list stored items, remove outdated entries, and account for propagation delay.

output_examples.input: I need image moderation in a Java backend.
output_examples.output: A concise design for sending local image bytes or a blob URL to Azure AI Content Safety and reviewing returned harm categories.

best_practices: Store API keys in environment variables or use managed identity where possible.
Request only the harm categories needed for your product policy and latency goals.
Validate severity thresholds with policy owners before blocking user content automatically.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding Content Safety keys or production endpoints in source control.
Using sample severity thresholds without testing them against real product policy.
Treating automated moderation scores as final decisions without review or appeal paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build Java applications that call Azure AI Content Safety for text moderation, image moderation, and blocklist management.

faq.question: Does it support image moderation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for analyzing image bytes from a file and images referenced by a blob URL.

faq.question: Does it cover custom blocklists?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows create, update, list, add item, remove item, and delete operations for text blocklists.

faq.question: Do I need Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples expect an Azure Content Safety endpoint and either an API key or DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that generate or explain Java SDK usage.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands on my machine?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation-only and contains Java examples; it does not include scripts that execute shell commands.
